solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Early music without instrumentation

parts.note: birdsong at first light is music sung at daybreak by many voices, with no instruments at all

explanation.surface: A concert of unaccompanied early vocal music.
explanation.definitionFit: The singing of birds at daybreak is a natural choir performing at the start of the day, entirely unaccompanied.

clue.text: Under the doctor, upset priest is easily managed

indicators.note: in a down entry the priest comes below the doctor

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A cleric under medical care, though distressed, is compliant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractable, submissive person or animal is easily managed.

clue.text: Presence of this person beset by anger

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the setter sits within the anger

parts.note: wrath is great anger
this person is the setter, I

explanation.surface: The setter feels the presence of their own fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presence' here means a ghostly being felt nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or spectre is an unseen presence, as in sensing a presence in the room.

clue.text: Some morticians trained to offer expressions of sympathy

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: Undertakers are taught to say comforting words.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of condolence offered to the unfortunate or bereaved are expressions of sympathy.

clue.text: Not awfully inspiring person given promotion as a commercial traveller?

indicators.note: awfully suggests the short word is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: a hero is an inspiring figure
an ad is a promotion, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A dull person gets a promotion and becomes a travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling salesman spends their working life travelling, idiomatically always away on business.

clue.text: Type of Christian turning up in certain universities

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A kind of Christian appears in some colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an Eastern church in communion with Rome while keeping its own rites.

clue.text: Early man discovered across Dorset/Hampshire border

indicators.note: the letters are found running across the join of the two county names, uncovered within them

explanation.surface: An early human fossil turned up on the border between two southern English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset and Hampshire are neighbouring counties on England's south coast; 'border' adds to the picture of the letters straddling the join.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the third son of Adam and Eve, one of the very first men.

clue.text: Eat to get over awful toil — having minimal energy, grow pale

indicators.note: the eat letters spread over the jumbled toil, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are made a mess of

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy, the least of it a single letter

explanation.surface: Eating to recover from exhausting work, lacking energy and turning pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns TOIL into TIOL, which EAT goes over; E (energy) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants kept from light become whitened and weak, so the verb means to blanch or lose colour.

clue.text: Multi-storey school needing extra money

parts.note: a high is a high school
a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: A tall school building needs more funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block of many floors is described as tall-built, a compound adjective.

clue.text: Act as desperate woman maybe, making terribly wooden response

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly scrambled

explanation.surface: A frantic woman acts, giving a stiff and wooden reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' means in urgent need of the lavatory; the definition is a polite euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy euphemism for a woman going to the lavatory, as one desperate to go might.

clue.text: Suffering at the back of cold entrance

indicators.note: the suffering piece is placed behind the cold piece

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
suffering is hurt or damage

explanation.surface: Being chilled after a cold front door causes misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, stressed on the second syllable: to bewitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or delight them, a verb sense meaning bewitch.

clue.text: Work that could get sewer functioning

definitions.text: Work that could get sewer functioning

parts.words: Work that could get sewer functioning
parts.note: a sewer here is someone who sews, not a drain, and this trade puts such a person to work

explanation.surface: Maintenance needed to get the drains working again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain but is one who sews, a needleworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting and stitching clothes to measure is the trade at which a needleworker is busy.

clue.text: Room seen through the French window

indicators.note: the room sits in the middle of the French article, so it shows through it

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
an attic is a room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: A room glimpsed through a window in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A window with small diamond panes set in a criss-cross frame of lead is a type of window.

clue.text: Feeble walker is old, retd, drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: An old retired person, unsteady on their feet after drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child just learning to walk totters unsteadily, so is a feeble walker.

clue.text: Devil on street with nasty stare kicks up a fuss

parts.note: a demon is a devil

indicators.note: nasty signals the letters of stare are turned into a nasty jumble

explanation.surface: A fiend on the street glares and makes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a public protest is to make a fuss about something.

clue.text: It's swell having tea thrown in for an extra amount

indicators.note: the tea is put inside the swell

parts.note: a surge is a swell, as of the sea
char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: It's a large wave with tea tossed in as a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional charge or levy on a bill is an extra amount to pay.

clue.text: Short gypsy dancing, girl revealed by telescope

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters move about into a new order
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A small Romany woman dancing is spotted through a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the final Y of GYPSY, and 'dancing' rearranges GYPS into SPYG.
explanation.definitionFit: A small handheld telescope, as used by a ship's lookout.

clue.text: Antioxidant from plant — the thing in the morning to be swallowed

indicators.note: the pieces are taken inside the plant

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
it means the thing
AM means in the morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: An antioxidant from a plant is just the thing to take each morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Tocopherol, found in vegetable oils, is a nutrient known for its antioxidant role.

clue.text: I phone darling, exuding love, naughtily flirting

indicators.note: naughtily signals the remaining letters behave badly and rearrange
exuding means giving off, so that letter leaves the words

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone rings their sweetheart, oozing affection, and flirts mischievously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' looks like affection, but it is the zero score in tennis; 'exuding' sheds that letter before 'naughtily' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser who chases many women is engaged in casual amorous dalliance, a synonym of flirting.

clue.text: Colour architect Jones used with encrusted diamonds

indicators.note: the architect is encrusted with the diamond, which sits inside his name

parts.note: Inigo Jones was the great English architect of the 17th century
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: An architect used a colour set with jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue-violet dye and the colour between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Church service with bread, one female getting huge piece of crust

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharist, where bread is consecrated
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A church service with bread, where a woman gets a huge bit of crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crust' looks like part of the loaf, but is the Earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact group of mountains forming a large block of the Earth's rocky outer layer.

clue.text: Billy may be so foolish

definitions.meaning: a billy is a male goat, so it would be like a goat
to act the goat is to play the fool, hence silly

explanation.definitionFit: Being like a goat covers a billy's nature and, by the idiom of acting the goat, silliness.

clue.text: Problem is hard, leading to irritation

indicators.note: the hard letter goes first, ahead of the irritation

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: A tough problem results in annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or hold-up is a difficulty, as in going off without a snag.

clue.text: Girl's shout of surprise seen on reflection as shout of praise

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name, with the possessive giving ANNAS
oh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A girl gasps in surprise and, thinking it over, cries out in praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of adoration used in Christian worship, as in hymns on Palm Sunday.

clue.text: Off-putting type offers ridiculous rationale

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are made absurd by being jumbled

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person gives a silly justification.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estranges or repels others is one who puts people off.

clue.text: American university map-maker passes over, misses out

indicators.note: the map-maker spreads over the university on both sides, enclosing it

parts.note: OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A US college's cartographer skips over parts and leaves things out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey (OS) makes Britain's official maps.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out or skip it is to drop it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Only part of play heard or watched

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a scene is a section of an act in a play

explanation.surface: Only some of the drama was listened to or viewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been observed or looked at has been viewed, the past participle of see.

clue.text: Party very loud after food, making one fed up

indicators.note: the party and loud pieces come after the food

parts.note: cheese is a kind of food
a do is a party
FF is fortissimo in music, very loud

explanation.surface: A noisy party following a meal leaves someone weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being annoyed or bored with something is an informal British idiom for disgruntled.
